summary: Keep mission human-gate alerts in Inbox by publishing full step-run identities

replay.detail: Gate claims and step paths are unchanged. Attention is derived from current reviews on read.

schema.detail: No stored-data migration: the faulty human-gate field is assembled on read, not persisted in the person/custom local_attention_open IVM families. Both public row serializers now receive the full step identity from their shared producer.

rules.detail: Review ownership, authority and gate decisions are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Human-gate attention step_run_id now contains the full step-run Id, matching source_id for step-owned gates. Loop-owned gates link their owning step and mission-owned gates omit the field. TypeScript schemas already require Id; web and mission consumers compare against full step ids. Swift treats the field as a string and presentation consumers derive the display path separately. No inspected TypeScript, iOS or TUI consumer requires the bare name. The reviews API keeps its separate display-path step field unchanged.

downtime.detail: Corrected rows are returned on the next read after the producer upgrade.

manual.detail: No operator action or client upgrade is required.

recovery.detail: No claims or persisted projections are rewritten.
